extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners referencing examiner procedures)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive examiner guidance from the MPEP on evaluating prior art, affidavits/declarations, file wrapper contents, classification, claim indexing, and documenting searches during patent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight of alleged copying in nonobviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged copying by a competitor is not persuasive of nonobviousness when the copy is not identical to the claimed product and the other manufacturer had not expended great effort to develop its own solution; copying can be persuasive where an admitted infringer failed to satisfactorily produce a solution after substantial effort and expense (e.g., 10 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite cases: Dow Chem. Co. v. American Cyanamid Co.; Pentec, Inc. v. Graphic Controls Corp.; Panduit Corp. v. Dennison Mfg. Co. Use factual details such as degree of similarity and the extent/duration of the competitor's efforts to assess weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of operability of cited patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent is presumed valid (35 U.S.C. 282), and that presumption includes a presumption of operability; examiners should not express opinions on operability of a patent reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations attacking operability must rebut the presumption by a preponderance of the evidence (In re Sasse). Examiners should defer to the presumption when evaluating references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumed enablement of processes to produce described products
rubrics_metrics.description: It is presumed that a process, if used by one skilled in the art, will produce the product or result described; this presumption is not overcome merely by showing it is possible to operate within the disclosure without obtaining the alleged product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider that skilled artisans are presumed to make routine experiments/adaptations; failures by uninterested experimenters carry little weight (In re Weber; In re Michalek; In re Reid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited effect of affidavits asserting inoperability of non-relied features
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an affidavit asserts inoperability in features of the reference which are not relied upon by the examiner, the reference remains effective as to other operative features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let assertions about unrelated inoperative features negate the utility of other enabling disclosures in the same reference (In re Shepherd).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must distinguish claims from alleged inoperative references
rubrics_metrics.description: If a presented affidavit asserts that the reference relied upon is inoperative, the claims represented by the applicant must distinguish from the alleged inoperative reference disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applicant's claims explicitly avoid the inoperative aspects identified; cite In re Crosby and related authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to require evidence of utility/operability for applicant's disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on when it is proper to require evidence of utility or operativeness and how to evaluate such evidence to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection (see MPEP § 2107.02 - § 2107.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer examiners to MPEP § 2107-series for legal precedent and procedural standards before demanding evidence of utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden after prima facie lack of enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the examiner establishes a prima facie case of lack of enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the burden shifts to the applicant to present persuasive arguments, supported by suitable proofs where necessary, that one skilled in the art could make and use the claimed invention using the disclosure as a guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant evidence must show enablement or that missing information was known to those of ordinary skill (In re Brandstadter; In re Howarth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations cannot substitute missing specification disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations presented to show that the disclosure of an application is sufficient to one skilled in the art are not acceptable to establish facts which the specification itself should recite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert testimony describing how to construct missing elements not recited in the application is generally insufficient to demonstrate that such construction was well-known (In re Buchner; In re Smyth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight of opinion testimony about disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion testimony that merely states a claim or count 'is disclosed' should not be given weight; testimony that explains the underlying factual basis for the opinion may be admitted and can be helpful, but its weight must be evaluated strictly case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Board guidance (Glaser v. Strickland) when admitting/examining expert opinion that purports to interpret a disclosure (see In re Oppenauer contrast).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of attribution affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain circumstances an affidavit or declaration may be submitted which attempts to attribute an activity, a reference or part of a reference to the applicant; if successful, the activity or reference is no longer applicable as a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.132 can attempt to show prior invention or derivation; see MPEP § 715 for procedures and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship designation and lack of presumption from authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation of authorship in a published article or inventorship in a patent or application publication does not create a presumption that the named author/inventor is the inventor of subject matter disclosed but not claimed so as to justify a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship inquiries may still be appropriate to clarify ambiguities; applicants must provide satisfactory showings to rebut rejections (In re Katz).

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfactory showing standard for rebutting inventorship-based rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: It is incumbent upon inventors named in the application to provide a satisfactory showing (e.g., via 37 CFR 1.132 affidavit) that the inventorship of the application is correct and that the reference derived from the applicant rather than from the author/patentee of the published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, uncontradicted 'unequivocal statement' from the applicant will generally be accepted but may be insufficient where contrary evidence exists (In re DeBaun; Ex parte Kroger; In re Carreira).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on using disclosure-derivation affidavits to gain publication date benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful 37 CFR 1.132 affidavit establishing derivation by the author/patentee of a first reference does not permit the applicant to assume that author's publication date for the purpose of defeating a later second reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow conversion of priority dates beyond what the affidavit legitimately establishes (In re Costello).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.130(a) conditions to disqualify commonly owned U.S. patent/app as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 on a U.S. patent or patent application publication that is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(b), and the claimed inventions are not identical but not patentably distinct and are owned by the same party, the applicant/owner may disqualify that patent or publication by submitting: (1) a terminal disclaimer under § 1.321(c); and (2) an oath or declaration stating current common ownership and that the inventor named in the application/patent is the prior inventor under 35 U.S.C. 104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration may be signed by inventor(s), attorney/agent of record, or assignee(s). Ensure requirements of §1.321(c) and 35 U.S.C. 104 are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting rejections and terminal disclaimer remedy (37 CFR 1.130(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application or patent under reexamination claims an invention not patentably distinct from an invention claimed in a commonly owned patent, a double patenting rejection will be made; a judicially-created double patenting rejection may be obviated by filing a terminal disclaimer under § 1.321(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 804.02 and related guidance on double patenting and terminal disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on establishing prior invention dates under 35 U.S.C. 104
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or patent owner may not establish a date of invention in a foreign country other than a NAFTA or WTO member country (or earlier than certain treaty dates for WTO/NAFTA members) for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (A) cannot establish invention date in a foreign country other than a NAFTA or WTO member; (B) cannot establish a date in a WTO member country other than a NAFTA country earlier than Jan 1, 1996; (C) cannot establish a date in a NAFTA country other than the U.S. earlier than Dec 8, 1993.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipating U.S. patent/publication cannot be disqualified as prior art under 103(c)/1.130/1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that anticipates the claimed subject matter cannot be disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) or 37 CFR 1.130 or 1.131.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not permit procedural devices to negate true anticipation by an earlier-published/issued U.S. reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: File wrapper contents — permanence and return policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that do not become a permanent part of the record should not be entered on the 'Contents' of the file wrapper. All papers legally entered on the 'Contents' receive a paper number and should not be withdrawn or returned without special authority; however, certain documents may be returned under 37 CFR 1.59 if unintentionally submitted or containing proprietary information not important to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.214 where appropriate; consult MPEP § 724 and § 604.04(a) for returnable documents and oath handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of papers in the file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: Until revision for allowance, applicant communications (specification, amendments, etc.) are fastened to the left side in inverse chronological order (latest on top); Office actions and other Office communications are fastened to the right side, with the drawing print always kept on top. At allowance, only papers required by the printer are placed on the left side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When duplicate amendments are submitted, handle duplicates per rules (destroy copy unless duplicate received within reply period and original late). Ensure drawing prints are kept accessible on right side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and endorsement of drawing prints
rubrics_metrics.description: Prints of drawings are fastened inside the file wrapper by the Office of Initial Patent Examination; white paper prints are kept on top of the papers on the right of the file wrapper. All prints and inked sketches subsequently filed should be endorsed with the application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 608.02(m) for print endorsement and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting data on the file wrapper label/bib-data
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner notices an error in data originally entered on the file wrapper or PALM bib-data sheet, make the correction in red ink and forward the application to TC technical support for correction of the PALM database and printing/placement of updated sheets or labels, with series-dependent procedures for 08/09/10-series applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common corrections include inventorship changes (37 CFR 1.48), filing date, prior U.S. application number errors, and benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c). Assignment name/address corrections go to Assignment Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling changes in inventor name, residence, or title
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between 'residence' and Post Office address. Unless specifically requested by applicant, the residence will not be changed on the file even if a new oath gives a different residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 605.02 and § 605.03 for procedure when applicant changes name; see § 605.04(c) for process steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording classification during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new application is received, note the classification and the initials/name of the examiner or docket designation in pencil on the file wrapper; keep notations current. Classification history box entries should indicate who reviewed the application, classes considered, and dates, and no other information is permitted there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to reduce needless routing and save time; consult MPEP § 903.07(a) regarding recording consultations in SEARCH NOTES when classification questions involve cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining the Index of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the Index of Claims up to date as a reliable index of all claims standing in an application and the amendment where they appear. Use the preprinted series for original claim numbers, place final patent claim numbers at allowance, designate independent claims by encircling claim number in red ink, draw red lines below numbers to indicate original and amended claim counts, and annotate rewritten claims with amendment identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claims are canceled draw a line through its number; indicate amendment letters beside the first claim of each amendment; do not strike original claim numbers even when rewritten—annotate (e.g., 'Amend. 1').

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of Search recording for first action and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits the examiner shall endorse, in black ink on the file wrapper, the classes/subclasses and other sources searched and the dates the search was conducted. For subsequent actions where search is updated, indicate that the search has been updated and identify additional fields of search; include databases and search queries/classifications used in the original search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take care to indicate precisely what was searched and when to provide a complete, accurate record of what was considered for each application (see MPEP § 904).

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCHED' box entry criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries to be printed on the patent front page are recorded in the 'SEARCHED' box: (A) complete search of a subclass (record class/subclass); (B) limited search of a subclass (record class/subclass and portion searched in parenthesis); (C) updates of previously made searches (record with '(updated)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (e.g., 424/270, 414/DIG.4, 424/270 (updated)). Search updates will be recorded but not printed; when updating from a parent application, indicate parent serial number or patent number.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCH NOTES' box entry criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries not printed on the patent but used to complete the record should be placed in 'SEARCH NOTES': (A) cursory scans (mark '(cursory)'), (B) consultations with other examiners (mark '(consulted)' and include name/art unit if desired), (C) searches of non-classified publications (record type, titles, periods), (D) searches of only publications in a subclass (mark '(publications only)'), (E) review of art cited in parent or related applications (record 'refs. checked' and application numbers), (F) computer/database searches (must document search logic, files searched/database name, date, and examiner initials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the minimum required data for each type; be specific for books/periodicals/catalogs. For computer searches, use printouts/forms or record info in SEARCH NOTES; see examples and STIC procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements for computer/database searches
rubrics_metrics.description: For computer-accessed text, chemical structure, or sequence databases, the examiner shall document: (1) the search logic/structure/sequence used as a query; (2) name of file(s) searched and database service; (3) date of the search; and (4) examiner's initials. Documentation can be via annotated printouts, PTO-1590 Search Request Form, or direct entry in the SEARCH NOTES box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the database history command omits elements, supplement the printout with missing elements or include the log off command to capture them. Circle the search statements whose results were reviewed, hole-punch printouts and place in the right-hand flap of the file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and filing of computer search printouts
rubrics_metrics.description: When using printouts as documentation, indicate which search statements were reviewed by circling them in black ink; hole-punch the form/printout pages with the required elements and place them in the application file on the right hand flap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the table of database-specific history commands and note any missing elements; supplement missing data by writing on the printout or including additional portions of the search transcript.
